sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
The week to 2026-09-04 was a rotation week, not a risk-off week and not a broad tech breakout. SPY returned just +0.1% over the window while dispersion beneath it was wide, and two facts rule out the easy readings: VIX at 14.32 (−0.88 pts) and high-yield spreads at 2.65% (−1 bp) say this was no growth scare, while the tech complex split hard enough — Memory/Storage +7.5% vs SPY against Cybersecurity −7.0% vs SPY — that "tech led" is also wrong. The index sat still; the money moved underneath it.

## Hardware and memory led; software and security lagged, inside the same tape
The steepest sector move was Memory/Storage, +7.6% on the week and +7.5% vs SPY with all four members priced (STX, WDC, MU, SNDK). Alongside it Computer/GPU rose +5.9% (+5.7% vs SPY, six of six priced) and Foundry +5.4% (+5.3% vs SPY, four of four). The plausible mechanism is an AI-hardware and memory-cycle bid concentrated in the physical build-out — silicon, storage, servers — rather than in the application layer. The single-name candidates trace the same edge: SNDK led the ranked stocks at +17.17% on the window (+17.06% vs SPY) and DELL +14.88% (+14.77% vs SPY), both hardware. SNDK's most recent report on 2026-08-05 (fiscal quarter ending 2026-06-30) posted actual EPS 38.82 against a 34.24 street mean, but that print is a month outside this window and cannot be this week's cause — the operating premise for the move is not in these payloads, so I hold it as an observation, not an explanation. Against that leadership, Cybersecurity fell −6.9% (−7.0% vs SPY, four of four priced) and Software/SaaS −4.7% (−4.8% vs SPY, six of six), with FIG −16.31% (−16.42% vs SPY), CDNS −14.01% and SNPS −11.02% among the week's worst ranked names. The read is not capital "leaving" software for hardware — returns do not trace transfers — but that the two ends of the same tech tape were priced on very different terms this week. Confirms if Memory/Storage holds its lead into next week's bars; refutes if the Semi-Cap/EDA drag (−1.5%, with CDNS and SNPS the anchors) spreads back into GPU and foundry names.

## Energy and the ag basket carried the macro-linked bid
Outside tech, XLE was the strongest sector at +2.1% vs SPY on the week (+11.8% vs SPY over four weeks), and WTI crude sat at 94.09 (+2.85%) in the post-window commodities snapshot — a same-direction cross-asset tell for the energy leadership, though that crude figure is a 2026-09-08 snapshot and not the week's change. The declared el-nino-ag-2026 theme was the single strongest line in rotation, its DBA/MOS/NTR/DE equal weight up +6.6% and +6.5% vs SPY on the week, with DE +10.03% (+9.92% vs SPY) and MOS +9.53% (+9.42% vs SPY) both showing in the ranked stocks. The theme's kill trigger — ONI below +0.5 two months running, or a 10% underperformance over 60 sessions — is not met, but I cannot verify its supporting ONI and CBOT inputs are satisfied without dated readings, so the entry rests on price this week, not confirmed weather data. Confirms if the ag basket holds its excess above SPY into next week; refutes if DE and MOS give back this week's lead and the basket's excess turns negative.

## Rates and policy did nothing to disturb the rotation
The macro backdrop was quiet enough to let the sector story run. Ten-year yields eased to 4.77% (−2 bp) into 2026-09-03, credit tightened a basis point to 2.65%, and the SPY gamma-flip level moved to 768.35 from a prior 770.19. The policy path carries a 9/16 hike probability of 55.7% as of 2026-09-04, but the frame excludes it from ranking for want of a prior observation, so I can quote the level and not its change — a coin-flip-plus reading on the September decision, no more. The front end and curve are dark this week: DGS2 was not ingested, so 2s10s cannot be computed and I state that rather than infer a shape. Nothing here contradicts the equity rotation; it simply did not drive it. Confirms a benign macro if the 9/16 probability prints again near 55.7 next week; refutes if the ten-year backs up through prior levels and credit widens together.

One coverage limitation: dated market observations for this window were unavailable — the reports store returned empty and the headline feed carried no history — so this article rests on the priced frame and rotation tables alone, with no narrative corroboration for any single-name move.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
Next week's question is whether the hardware-over-software split that defined the week to 2026-09-04 is a durable cycle tell or a one-week dispersion spike. Memory/Storage (+7.5% vs SPY), Computer/GPU (+5.7%) and Foundry (+5.3%) all led on the same theme — the physical AI build-out — and the cleanest confirmation is simple persistence: if those three hold positive excess vs SPY into next week's bars while Semi-Cap/EDA (−1.5%) stops dragging, the rotation is real. The reverse risk is that the EDA weakness in CDNS and SNPS is the leading edge of a broader semi de-rating that eventually reaches the GPU and foundry names now leading; watch whether Semi-Cap/EDA's excess turns less negative or more.

The software and cybersecurity laggards (−4.8% and −7.0% vs SPY) are the other side of the same trade. FIG's −16.42% vs SPY is the standout, but with no dated operating fact behind it I treat the whole cohort as priced-weak, not fundamentally broken — a bounce here is as consistent with the tape as continued weakness, and I hold no directional view until a name-level catalyst lands.

Energy and the ag basket are the macro-linked persisters. XLE's +2.1% vs SPY on the week sits on top of +11.8% over four weeks, the most durable cross-window strength in the sector table, and crude near 94.09 supports it. The el-nino-ag-2026 theme led all of rotation at +6.5% vs SPY; its kill trigger is not met, but its ONI and CBOT premises are unverified in these payloads, so the position rests on price. It confirms if the basket holds excess above SPY; it invalidates on a 10% underperformance over 60 sessions or two months of ONI below +0.5 — neither observable yet.

Macro should stay in the background. Ten-year at 4.77%, credit at 2.65% and VIX at 14.32 describe a calm backdrop, but I draw no complacency inference from low vol and tight spreads alone — they are observations. The one dated forward marker is the 9/16 hike decision, which is later context, not next week's event; the 55.7% probability is a level without a change, so I watch for a re-print rather than call its direction. The nearer risk is that ADBE's post-close report lands mid-week and repriced the software cohort either way.

That is the only admitted forward catalyst inside seven days and it lands as a software print into a week where that cohort was the laggard, so the reaction reads across the rest of the group. No consensus or prior figures are supplied on the row beyond the implied move, and no other event is admitted in the window — the 9/16 policy decision is later context, not a coming-week catalyst.
